picks.what: View of the town on the Dâmbovița, print published in Leipzig
picks.why: earliest general view, labeled BUCHOREST, churches and princely court along the river

picks.what: View over the rooftops from the Colțea Tower, painting (Bucharest Metropolitan Library)
picks.why: color general view of the old city with its church towers

picks.what: Aerial photograph of the city center and Cișmigiu Park, taken by the German army
picks.why: high-resolution aerial of the center with Cișmigiu Park and the Dâmbovița; ordinary city, not war damage

picks.what: The Palace of the Parliament seen from the Metropolitan Hill, photograph
picks.why: the city’s best-known landmark above the rooftops

gaps: P0, P1: none. P3: only #3, a single church (1845 book illustration), skipped. P6 photo is ordinary in quality.
notes: P4 alternative: #4 (1890s photochrom general view with St. Spyridon) is equally good; #8 chosen for its earlier date and wider spread. #13 is a smaller copy of #12 (dated 1916 there). #10 (1865) shows the flood, an event. #9 (1864 Szathmari photo panorama) is too thin (7:1). #12’s source dates it 1916–18; Commons says probably before the Battle of Bucharest, Nov–Dec 1916. #8 medium inferred from appearance (Preziosi’s 1868 Bucharest watercolors); Commons files it under engravings.
